Rules, and they are not negotiable:

messages.content:
Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: road-trip
Leaving from: Montréal, Québec
Going to: Gaspésie
Dates: 2027-07-03 to 2027-07-11, fixed
Travellers: 4
Ages that change the plan: 41, 39, 11, 7
Access needs: not answered
Budget: 4200 CAD, total
Appetite for effort: moderate
Roughest night they will accept: simple
Would rule the trip out: No more than one night in any campground without showers

About this road-trip:
How much road a day holds: half-day
Vehicle: car
Whose vehicle: own
Route style: loop
Stops they already want: Percé Rock, Forillon National Park
In their words: The seven-year-old is miserable after about three hours in the car, so we would rather stop often than push through. We have done the north shore before and would like to see something new.

candidates.title: Boat cruise around Percé Rock and Bonaventure Island
candidates.summary: Covers the requested Percé Rock stop up close by boat, with a landing on Bonaventure Island for the northern gannet colony. The walk to the colony is a few kilometres each way, which suits moderate effort and an active 7-year-old. Access needs were not answered, so trail and boat accessibility is not accounted for.

candidates.title: Percé Rock low-tide walk
candidates.summary: At low tide you can walk the beach out toward the base of Percé Rock. It is free, short and flexible around the boat trip. It depends on tide timing, which was not checked here.

candidates.title: Percé glass walkway lookout
candidates.summary: A glass platform on a clifftop gives a view over Percé and the rock. It is a manageable hike or shuttle for kids. Hours and access were not verified.

candidates.title: Cap-Gaspé Les Graves trail, Forillon
candidates.summary: This coastal trail in Forillon, one of the requested stops, runs to the lighthouse at Land's End. Seals and whales are often seen along the way. The full trail may be long for a 7-year-old, so a shorter out-and-back works. Park entry is charged separately.

place.name: Les Graves trail, Forillon National Park

candidates.title: Whale-watching cruise from Grande-Grave
candidates.summary: Whale-watching boats leave from inside Forillon and are a highlight for kids. Minimum age rules and how the family handles seasickness were not checked.

candidates.title: Parc national de Miguasha fossil site
candidates.summary: This UNESCO fossil site sits on the southern Baie-des-Chaleurs side, so it is new ground for a family that has done the north shore. It has a museum and a beach walk, and it makes a good short stop that breaks up the drive.

candidates.title: Site historique du Banc-de-Pêche-de-Paspébiac
candidates.summary: A heritage fishing site on the south coast with costumed guides, suited to kids. It is a natural stop between long drives.
